The weights of watermelons produced by a certain farm are normally distributed with a mean of 4.82 kg. Long-term quality control data show that when a watermelon from this farm is randomly selected, the probability that it weighs less than 3.75 kg is $0.116$.

A watermelon is labelled as being the ideal size if it weighs between 4.82 kg and 5.89 kg.

The normal distribution is symmetric about the mean $4.82$, and $3.75$ and $5.89$ are the same distance from it:
$$4.82-3.75=1.07=5.89-4.82$$
So, by symmetry, $P(X>5.89)=P(X<3.75)=0.116$.

Half of the distribution lies above the mean, so
$$\begin{aligned} P(4.82<X<5.89)&=0.5-P(X>5.89)\\ &=0.5-0.116\\ &=0.384\end{aligned}$$
